title: Base change for open-closed immersions
statement:
Let $j:U\to X$ be both an open and a closed immersion of schemes
and let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism, forming the
cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_XU&\xrightarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle g}\\
U&\xrightarrow{\;j\;}&X .
\end{array}
$$

Then for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$ the base change map
$g^{-1}j_*F\to h_*p^{-1}F$ of
[def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $U'=Y\times_XU$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $j$ identifies $U$ with an open subscheme of $X$; by [def-weil-closed-immersion] its image is closed, so $V=X\setminus j(U)$ is also open. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $h:U'\to Y$ is an open immersion. The pullback property [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] identifies its image with $g^{-1}(j(U))$: a morphism to $Y$ whose composite with $g$ factors through $U$ has a unique lift to $U'$. In particular, for a geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$ with $\bar x=g\bar y$, if $x\in j(U)$ then there are unique lifts $\bar u$ to $U$ and $\bar t$ to $U'$, with $p\bar t=\bar u$ and $h\bar t=\bar y$. Otherwise $y\in g^{-1}(V)$, an open disjoint from $U'$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the blueprint first case distinction: Stacks 01HE (definition-immersion-locally-ringed-spaces), 01HK (definition-closed-immersion-locally-ringed-spaces), 01IO (definition-immersion), and 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), open-immersion case.

proof.text:
Suppose $x\in j(U)$, and use the geometric points of step 1. The inverse-image stalk comparison [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], first for $g$ and then for $j$, and the counit isomorphism $j^{-1}j_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ from [lem-kun-open-immersion-restriction], identify
$$ (g^{-1}j_*F)_{\bar y}\cong(j_*F)_{\bar x}\cong F_{\bar u}. $$
Applying the same open-immersion counit isomorphism to $h$ and the inverse-image stalk comparison to $h$ and $p$ identifies
$$ (h_*p^{-1}F)_{\bar y}\cong(p^{-1}F)_{\bar t}\cong F_{\bar u}. $$
These open-immersion isomorphisms are the restriction counits: on an etale object over the open, direct image evaluates on that same object. Thus the indicated identifications send a represented germ to its restriction at the lifted point.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3) and its direct colimit proof; Tag 03PY (definition-direct-image-sheaf); Tag 0F70 (lemma-jshriek-open), the restriction counit for an open immersion.

proof.text:
Under the two identifications of step 2, the specified exchange map is the identity. Indeed, by [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] a germ of $j_*F$ at $\bar x$ is represented by a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar x$ and $s\in(j_*F)(W)=F(W\times_XU)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The germ comparison [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] for $g$ says that its inverse image is represented by the unit pullback of $s$ on $W_Y=Y\times_XW$, pointed by $(\bar y,\bar w)$. The representative formula in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] sends this section to its inverse-image section on
$$ U'\times_YW_Y\cong U'\times_U(U\times_XW). $$
At the lifted point, the germ comparison for $p$ sends this section back to the germ of the original $s$ at $(\bar u,\bar w)$ in $U\times_XW$. This is exactly the image of the original germ under the source identification of step 2. Every source germ has such a representative, so the map on stalks is the identity on $F_{\bar u}$, hence is invertible.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), direct proof and compatibility with the inverse-image unit; Tag 03PY (definition-direct-image-sheaf); expansion of the fixed exchange map from the blueprint.

proof.text:
Suppose $x\notin j(U)$. For a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar x$, replace it by $W_V=W\times_XV$. This is still an etale neighbourhood of $\bar x$: $V\to X$ is an etale object by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and the fibre product is an object of the same small etale site by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The lift of $\bar x$ to $V$ and $\bar w$ give its pointing, and the projection $W_V\to W$ is a pointed neighbourhood morphism. Thus every section on $W$ has the same germ as its restriction to $W_V$ in the defining stalk colimit [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. On each such neighbourhood, [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives
$$ (j_*F)(W_V)=F(W_V\times_XU)=F(\varnothing)=0. $$
Here the middle fibre product is empty since $V$ is disjoint from $j(U)$, and the empty covering in the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] gives $F(\varnothing)=0$. Thus $(j_*F)_{\bar x}=0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] for $g$ gives $(g^{-1}j_*F)_{\bar y}=0$. For the target, put $C=g^{-1}(V)$, the open neighbourhood of $y$ disjoint from $U'$ in step 1. Given a pointed etale neighbourhood $(T,\bar t_0)$ of $\bar y$, the fibre product $T_C=T\times_Y C$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Its projection to $T$ is a neighbourhood refinement. Since $T_C\times_Y U'=\varnothing$, the direct-image formula gives $(h_*p^{-1}F)(T_C)=(p^{-1}F)(\varnothing)=0$, again by the empty covering sheaf axiom. Every section on $T$ therefore represents the zero germ after this refinement, proving $(h_*p^{-1}F)_{\bar y}=0$. The exchange stalk map is therefore the unique map $0\to0$, an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion), proof of the outside case; Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback); Tag 02GP (morphisms-lemma-open-immersion-etale); Tag 021D (topologies-lemma-fibre-products-etale).

proof.text: Every geometric point of $Y$ falls into one of the two cases of step 1. The actual exchange map is invertible at these stalks by steps 3 and 4, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes it an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. If $Y$ is empty there are no geometric points and the same conservativity statement applies vacuously. If $U$ is empty only step 4 occurs; if $U=X$ only steps 2 and 3 occur.
